trust_decision.summary: Which Python SSLContext the C servername callback may treat as alive: at the pinned commit it trusts the borrowed SSL_CTX servername arg (the context that installed the callback), which OpenSSL can still reach through the connection's session_ctx after sni_callback switched the socket's context and the original PySSLContext was freed.

landing_point.why: The summary names sni_callback; _servername_callback is the only C function invoking it, and it casts the borrowed args pointer to PySSLContext.

fix_sites.entry_point: server-side handshake (SSLSocket.do_handshake / SSLObject.do_handshake via SSLContext.wrap_socket/wrap_bio with sni_callback set); context switch via SSLSocket/SSLObject.context setter
deallocation of an ssl.SSLContext (last reference dropped, e.g. after socket.context reassignment)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All sites are in Modules/_ssl.c; the nearest 'looks out of scope' site is the teardown path context_dealloc at Modules/_ssl.c:3181-3191, which is not one of the listed kinds.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver who adds Py_INCREF on sslctx inside _servername_callback can argue the dealloc/setter change is unnecessary because 'the callback now holds a reference', missing that on the HelloRetryRequest re-entry the args pointer is already dangling before the callback starts.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: SNI virtual hosting: sni_callback must still be able to reassign sslobj.context (the socket must switch to the leaf context and the dispatch context must be collectable afterwards); a fix that refuses the context switch, keeps the original context alive from the socket, or disables SNI after a switch breaks this. Published fix also changes semantics so later ClientHellos dispatch to the new context's sni_callback.

O6_input_shapes: callback switches context, drops the original and raises (error path reads sslctx->set_sni_cb after the call)
callback switches context and returns None, followed by a TLS 1.3 HelloRetryRequest second ClientHello (callback re-entered with a dangling args pointer)
servername present vs NULL (two call sites of the Python callback)
callback returning an int alert code vs None

O7_producer.where: The dangling state is OpenSSL's session_ctx keeping the original SSL_CTX (with servername arg) after SSL_set_SSL_CTX at Modules/_ssl.c:2148; this is library-internal, not a listed producer kind.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: ALPN select callback also receives a borrowed PySSLContext as its arg (set at Modules/_ssl.c:3322); a planted variant consulting the session/original context instead of SSL_get_app_data(s)->ctx would mirror the bug.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same 'pass self as callback arg' idiom as the SNI setter; a maintainer would naturally write it this way.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: msg_callback calls ssl_obj->ctx->msg_cb as a borrowed reference while running Python code that may reassign sslobj.context; a planted variant could cache the context or callback across the call.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same borrowed-callback pattern the published fix replaced with Py_XNewRef(sni_cb) in _servername_callback; lives in a separate file of the same module.

O9_family: memory safety: use-after-free (object lifetime of a borrowed C callback argument, CWE-416)

O10_build.toolchain: autoconf ./configure && make; requires OpenSSL dev headers with TLS 1.3 (HRR test uses set_ecdh_curve('secp384r1'))
O10_build.project_tests: Lib/test/test_ssl.py SSLObjectTests (MemoryBIO-based, offline); fix adds test_sni_callback_context_released_and_callback_raises and test_sni_callback_context_released_before_second_client_hello (fix.diff:10250-10328)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Py_INCREF the args-derived sslctx at the top of _servername_callback (or make the socket hold the original context), which misses the HRR re-entry with an already-freed arg or breaks the collectability of the dispatch context.

out_of_scope_notes: The fix diff bundles unrelated release changes (asyncio, tarfile, urllib.request docs, other gh issues); only the gh-156293 hunks were used.
Lib/ssl.py:498-502 shim_cb closure references the context itself (reference cycle ctx->set_sni_cb->shim_cb->ctx), which keeps legacy-API users' contexts alive until GC; not pursued.
unverified: That OpenSSL dispatches the servername callback via session_ctx and ALPN via the current ctx is taken from the fix's own comment (fix.diff:10381-10388) and general OpenSSL knowledge, not from code in this tree.
Whether the msg_callback borrowed call (Modules/_ssl/debughelpers.c:70-75) is actually reachable as a UAF was not established; listed only as injection room.
present_in_latest not applicable: no O8 routes and no latest release supplied.
